title: Rembrandt, Michelangelo and a love of history
summary: Edison says he loves art and European history and dislikes how Indians are shown in American history and film.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: When did you start to get interested in paintings and museums and historic buildings and everything?
Oh, I've always been an admirer of the arts, you know. I've been a Rembrandt fan for years.
You just like to look at them, to start with.

You know, it's amazing how something can look and have its beauty hundreds of years later, you know, and the forethought of what he did, you know, like how many years he was ahead of his time, you know. And Michelangelo, I was in Italy at the Sistine Chapel, and those frescoes in there that he painted. Oh, my goodness. And they're still in existence, you know? And I've always -- I majored in history in school and I've always --
Well, we are living in history.
Well, that's true, but when you say 'history,' you mean past history.

Oh, yeah, past history. I like European history. I didn't care too much for American history because they never -- the only American is the Indian and you very seldom read anything about the Indian in history, no more than being inhuman. And if you see all the movies, they would take ten white soldiers, they would wipe out 10,000 Indians, you know? They were always losing. And the only ones that they won, battle that they won, was Little Big Horn, when they wiped out General Custer, you know. They had to make that authentic because there was nobody else living to say any different, you know? So --
Yeah, they always are ridiculous, you know.
